subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures remain an accepted async run that terminalizes visibly, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight sandbox startup and reject before returning `accepted`?
rationale: That choice changes the public spawn timing contract and lifecycle/session semantics, not only a local Docker error string.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` non-blocking but emit/log a typed startup failure that updates session and subagent state when Docker startup fails.

options.title: Preflight before accepted
options.body: Start or validate the sandbox before returning `accepted`, trading clearer immediate failure for extra latency and a stricter spawn contract.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle tracker
options.body: Use this issue as the sandbox proof case while the broader lifecycle contract is resolved in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` non-blocking but emit/log a typed startup failure that updates session and subagent state when Docker startup fails.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history spans subagent spawn, sandbox/runtime docs, terminal outcome precedence, and gateway wait/session lifecycle surfaces.
